angrahed/tradescrapr.readmeHtml:
A resumable UN Comtrade scraper built for unattended operation, with two modes:

  1. Targeted scrapes — expand a YAML spec into a persistent task queue that can run for days or weeks within the free tier's ~500 calls/day quota, surviving kills, reboots, and quota exhaustion.
  2. Monthly monitor — a cron/launchd job that detects newly published (or re-published) monthly data via the free availability endpoint and scrapes exactly that, at full detail.

Plus a full-screen interactive job builder (just run tradescrapr) to pick exactly what to download, and a live terminal dashboard (tradescrapr ui) to watch it work.

Key properties

  • Resume-by-default: every task is idempotent and checkpointed in SQLite; kill -9, reboot, or quota exhaustion never loses work — just run again.
  • Quota-aware: a persistent daily-call ledger budgets 450 of the free tier's 500 calls, sleeps until the reset, and resyncs if the server disagrees.
  • Cap-aware: responses that hit the per-call record cap split automatically (flow → partner groups sized from the availability endpoint's record counts → HS-chapter batches) and the children are tracked as ordinary tasks.
  • Revision-aware: when a reporter re-publishes a month, the monitor wipes and re-scrapes that partition and cancels any stale queued tasks for it.
  • Clean data: hive-partitioned parquet with pinned dtypes (HS codes stay strings — no leading-zero corruption) and a provenance manifest per chunk.
  • Free and premium: one tier switch; premium keys use whole-file bulk downloads instead of paged calls.

Requirements

  • Linux or macOS (Windows unsupported — the locking and dashboard are POSIX). CI runs the full suite on both.
  • uv (manages Python 3.12 and all dependencies; you never need pip or a system Python).
  • A UN Comtrade API key — free, see next section.

Install

git clone https://github.com/angrahed/tradescrapr.git
cd tradescrapr
uv sync                        # creates .venv, installs pinned dependencies
uv run tradescrapr --version   # sanity check
uv run tradescrapr refs refresh  # cache reporter/partner/HS reference data (no key needed)

API key

Getting a free key

  1. Register (free) at https://comtradeplus.un.org.
  2. Sign in to the developer portal at https://comtradedeveloper.un.org with the same account, go to Products, and subscribe to the free API product.
  3. Your subscription key appears under your profile. That's the key you give tradescrapr.

Providing the key

tradescrapr reads, in order of preference:

  1. the COMTRADE_API_KEY environment variable — set it in your shell, crontab, systemd unit, or launchd plist and everything just works:

    export COMTRADE_API_KEY="your-key-here"

  2. a .env file at the project root (cp .env.example .env and fill it in). A real environment variable wins over .env for the same name.

The legacy name COMTRADE_KEY is also accepted. The key is only ever sent as a request header — it never appears in URLs, logs, manifests, or the state database, and .env is gitignored.

Public repo safety

Do not commit real API keys, .env, downloaded data, SQLite state, or logs. The default .gitignore excludes .env, data/, state/, logs/, caches, and the virtual environment. .env.example intentionally contains only the placeholder COMTRADE_API_KEY=your-key-here.

Free vs. premium

Free Premium Individual Premium Institutional
Cost $0 $2,000/yr $6,000–12,000/yr
Calls/day 500 (tradescrapr budgets 450) 5,000 unlimited
Records/call 100,000 250,000 250,000
Bulk files — ✓ ✓

Free tier is comfortable for the ongoing monthly monitor (~1–2 days of quota per new month) and fine for the default 2024+ backfill (~3–6 weeks). Deep historical backfills are premium territory (days instead of months via bulk files). Premium is sold through shop.un.org / subscriptions@un.org; a free 15-business-day trial exists, and institutions often already hold a site license — check before buying.

With a premium key, set tier: premium in config.yaml: the record cap rises, the daily budget lifts, and the monitor switches to bulk-file downloads automatically.

Quickstart: the smoke test

Before trusting a long run, spend ~6 quota calls verifying everything end to end:

uv run tradescrapr plan jobs/smoke.yaml --dry-run   # 4 tasks, nothing written
uv run tradescrapr plan jobs/smoke.yaml
uv run tradescrapr run
uv run tradescrapr status                            # expect 4/4 done

You should find four parquet files with manifests under data/raw/comtrade/final/freq=A/period=2022/.

Interactive job builder

The quickest way to set up a download is the full-screen interactive form — just start tradescrapr:

uv run tradescrapr        # in a terminal, opens the job builder
uv run tradescrapr new    # same thing, explicit

Pick reporters/partners/commodities from searchable lists (space toggles, * selects all). In reporter, partner, and commodity-code pickers, I imports the selection from a .txt, .csv, or .json list. Set periods and flows, and watch the live task/quota estimate. s saves the spec to jobs/<name>.yaml, plans the job, and then offers to start the worker or open the dashboard. The saved YAML is a normal job spec — everything below applies to it.

Import file formats

Picker imports replace the current selection. They validate every identifier before applying anything, so a file with one unknown country or product code leaves the picker unchanged.

Supported formats:

  • .txt: identifiers separated by newlines, commas, semicolons, or whitespace.
  • .csv: the first non-empty column from each row; a header such as code, country_code, iso3, product_code, or hs_code is ignored.
  • .json: an array of identifiers, an array of objects with keys such as code, id, iso3, cmdCode, or product_code, or an object containing a list under codes, reporters, partners, commodities, or products.

Reporters and partners may be ISO3 or numeric Comtrade codes. Commodity imports must match codes in the selected classification, and leading zeroes are kept.

Targeted mode

Job specs live in jobs/*.yaml:

name: eu3_hs6_annual
dataset: final            # final | tariffline
type: C                   # C goods, S services
freq: A                   # A annual, M monthly
classification: HS
reporters: [DEU, FRA, ITA]   # ISO3 / numeric codes, or "all"
partners: all
flows: [M, X]
commodities: {level: 6}   # or {codes: [870321, "8703", TOTAL]}
periods: "2015:2024"      # ranges/lists; monthly like "202001:202412"
breakdown: classic        # classic = totals over partner2/customs/transport-mode
                          # full  = every breakdown (~10x the rows)
uv run tradescrapr plan jobs/eu3_hs6_annual.yaml    # create job + tasks (idempotent)
uv run tradescrapr run                              # work the queue; running IS resuming
uv run tradescrapr status --verbose                 # progress, quota burn, dead tasks
uv run tradescrapr retry-dead                       # revive dead tasks after fixing causes

Planning is idempotent (the job id hashes the spec), and with reporters: all only reporter-periods that actually exist are enqueued. One task = one reporter × period × flow at the requested commodity detail; oversized responses split automatically. run accepts --job, --max-calls, --stop-after HOURS, and --no-wait-quota (exit instead of sleeping at quota exhaustion).

Command reference

Command Purpose
tradescrapr / tradescrapr new Open the interactive job builder
tradescrapr refs refresh Refresh cached reporter, partner, and HS reference data
tradescrapr plan jobs/<spec>.yaml Expand a job spec into persistent tasks
tradescrapr plan jobs/<spec>.yaml --dry-run Preview task expansion without writing state
tradescrapr run Work queued tasks, resuming any interrupted job
tradescrapr status --verbose Show job/task progress and dead-task details
tradescrapr retry-dead Requeue dead tasks after fixing the underlying issue
tradescrapr monitor --dry-run Preview new/revised monthly releases
tradescrapr monitor Enqueue and scrape new/revised monthly releases
tradescrapr ui Open the live read-only dashboard
tradescrapr da --period 202405 --reporter DEU Inspect Comtrade availability rows

Long unattended runs

nohup uv run tradescrapr run >> logs/nohup.log 2>&1 &

or, surviving reboots on Linux, ~/.config/systemd/user/tradescrapr-run.service:

[Unit]
Description=tradescrapr targeted worker

[Service]
Type=exec
WorkingDirectory=%h/main/projects/tradescrapr
Environment=COMTRADE_API_KEY=your-key-here
ExecStart=%h/main/projects/tradescrapr/.venv/bin/tradescrapr run
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=60

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
systemctl --user enable --now tradescrapr-run.service
loginctl enable-linger $USER   # keep user services alive after logout

Monitor mode

uv run tradescrapr monitor --dry-run    # show the new/revised release diff
uv run tradescrapr monitor              # scrape it

Each run diffs the free availability listing against the local releases table: unseen reporter-periods are new; a newer lastReleased timestamp is a revision (partition wiped and re-scraped, stale queued tasks cancelled). A release is only marked done when every one of its tasks finished, so interrupted runs resume on the next scheduled tick. Scope lives in the monitor: block of config.yaml — start_period bounds the first-run backfill.

Schedule it daily (releases trickle in all month). Linux crontab:

17 6 * * * cd $HOME/main/projects/tradescrapr && /usr/bin/flock -n state/monitor.cron.lock .venv/bin/tradescrapr monitor >> logs/cron.log 2>&1

(macOS scheduling below.)

Dashboard

uv run tradescrapr ui            # live full-screen dashboard (q quits, r refreshes)
uv run tradescrapr ui --once     # one static snapshot (pipe-friendly)

An htop-style view: quota gauge with a 7-day burn sparkline and time-to-reset, per-job progress bars with ETA, what the worker is fetching right now, the monitor's release backlog by period, a live color-coded activity feed, and dead tasks front and center. It is a read-only observer — run it in a second tmux pane or SSH session while a worker is going; the header shows whether a worker currently holds the lock.

Data layout & provenance

data/raw/comtrade/{final|tariffline}/freq={A|M}/period={p}/reporter={code}/
    part-{task_id}[-{seq}].parquet
    part-{task_id}[-{seq}].parquet.manifest.json

Read it with pl.scan_parquet("data/raw/comtrade/final/**/*.parquet") — the hive keys become columns. Every *Code column and period is pinned to string (HS codes keep leading zeros); values are Float64. Each chunk's manifest records the source URL, query parameters, row count, sha256, timestamp, and citation — enough to audit or rebuild any partition.

Configuration

config.yaml at the project root; every key optional. Precedence: CLI flags > TRADESCRAPR_* env vars > config.yaml > defaults.

Block Highlights
tier free (default) or premium
api rps, max_records, timeout_s (defaults follow the tier)
quota daily_budget (450 free), reset_time/reset_tz (00:00 UTC)
retry transport retries, task max attempts, backoff, split depth
planner max_cmd_codes_per_call, combine_flows
monitor datasets, freq, cmd_level, breakdown, start_period, reporter filter
paths data/state/logs locations

macOS

Everything works identically on macOS — locking, signals, atomic writes, and the dashboard are plain POSIX, and CI runs the full suite on macos-latest. Two platform notes:

  • Scheduling: macOS has no /usr/bin/flock binary and launchd is the native scheduler. Either drop the flock -n ... prefix from the crontab line (safe — the app-level state/worker.lock already prevents overlapping runs), or use a LaunchAgent at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/org.tradescrapr.monitor.plist:

    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN"
  "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>org.tradescrapr.monitor</string>
  <key>WorkingDirectory</key><string>/Users/YOU/main/projects/tradescrapr</string>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  <dict><key>COMTRADE_API_KEY</key><string>your-key-here</string></dict>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/Users/YOU/main/projects/tradescrapr/.venv/bin/tradescrapr</string>
    <string>monitor</string>
  </array>
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key>
  <dict><key>Hour</key><integer>6</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>17</integer></dict>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/Users/YOU/main/projects/tradescrapr/logs/cron.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/Users/YOU/main/projects/tradescrapr/logs/cron.log</string>
</dict>
</plist>

    Load with launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/org.tradescrapr.monitor.plist. (A .env file at the project root works too, since WorkingDirectory is set.)

  • Laptop sleep: wrap long foreground runs in caffeinate -i uv run tradescrapr run so idle sleep doesn't pause the worker. Interrupted runs resume anyway; this just avoids the pause.

Recovery cheatsheet

Symptom Action
VM rebooted / process killed just run again — resume is the default
status --verbose shows dead tasks read last_error; retry-dead after fixing
Quota confusion after key change server 403s resync the ledger automatically
Fresh scrape of a partition wanted re-plan an edited spec (new job id), or delete the job's rows and partition dir
Two workers by accident impossible: state/worker.lock (flock) is exclusive

Never run two workers against different checkouts sharing one state/ — the lock is per-file. data/, state/, logs/, and .env are gitignored; back up state/ alongside data/ when archiving a scrape (it is the record of what was fetched when).

Development

uv run pytest              # full suite, no network needed
uv run ruff check src tests
uv run ruff format src tests

CI (GitHub Actions) runs lint + tests on Ubuntu and macOS for every push and PR.

angrahed/EBRDo.description: Harmonize countries in the EBRD style, with the same tool in Julia, R, and Stata, from one source of truth.
angrahed/EBRDo.readmeHtml:
Harmonize countries in the EBRD style. Available in Julia, R, Python, and Stata.

EBRDo takes a table with a country column (ISO2, ISO3, ISO-numeric, or country name) and adds five columns that classify each country the way the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) does. The same tool is available in all four languages, generated from one source of truth and tested to give identical results.

# R
library(EBRDo)
ebrdo(data.frame(country = c("Kazakhstan", "Germany", "Kosovo", "United States")))
#>         country ebrd_coo     ebrd_name          ebrd_region   transition_group  combined_group
#> 1    Kazakhstan        1    Kazakhstan         Central Asia       Central Asia            <NA>
#> 2       Germany        0       Germany      Advanced Europe    Advanced Europe Advanced Europe
#> 3        Kosovo        1        Kosovo South-eastern Europe    Western Balkans EBRD Emerging…
#> 4 United States        0 United States                 <NA>               <NA>            <NA>

What it adds

Column Meaning
ebrd_coo 1 if the country is an EBRD Country of Operation, 0 otherwise, missing if unresolved
ebrd_name EBRD-spelled English name (Czechia, Türkiye, Taipei China, Hong Kong SAR, West Bank and Gaza, …)
ebrd_region Official EBRD region group (CEB, Central Asia, EEC, South-eastern Europe, SEMED, Türkiye, SSA)
transition_group The grouping used in EBRD's Transition Report (EBRD-EU, Western Balkans, …)
combined_group A single collapsed grouping (EBRD-EU / EBRD Emerging Europe / advanced / IMF EMMIEs / IMF LIDCs)

Non-COO comparator groups (Advanced Europe, Advanced Economies, the IMF aggregates, EBRD Emerging Europe) can be placed alongside the EBRD groups, and are configurable. Ireland is always excluded from comparators, because multinational profit-shifting distorts its macro data. Selecting overlapping comparator groups raises an informative error.

The four ports

Julia R Python Stata
Folder julia/ r/ python/ stata/
Works with any Tables.jl table data.frame, tibble, data.table, duckdb pandas DataFrame the in-memory dataset
Harmonization engine CountryCodes.jl countrycode (CRAN) country_converter bundled crosswalk
Entry point ebrdo(table, :col) df %>% ebrdo() ebrdo.ebrdo(df) ebrdo var

One source of truth, verified parity

All ports derive their reference data from a single curated definition built on countrycode/CountryCodes/country_converter. That definition covers the 41 Countries of Operation, the EBRD/Transition/IMF groupings, the special spellings, and the Kosovo handling. The Stata crosswalk and the Julia/R/Python lookup tables are all generated from it. A cross-port parity test runs the same adversarial inputs (mixed schemes, accents, whitespace, Kosovo aliases, numerics, unresolvable values) through the ports and confirms they return identical classifications, value for value. None of them crash, and none corrupt their input. (The Python port resolves names through country_converter; a few non-COO fallback spellings can differ from countrycode — see python/README.md.)

Installation

Julia

using Pkg
Pkg.add(url = "https://github.com/angrahed/CountryCodes.jl")          # dependency, until registered
Pkg.add(url = "https://github.com/angrahed/EBRDo", subdir = "julia")

R

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("angrahed/EBRDo/r")
# or:  remotes::install_github("angrahed/EBRDo", subdir = "r")

Python

uv add "ebrdo @ git+https://github.com/angrahed/EBRDo#subdirectory=python"
# or:  pip install "git+https://github.com/angrahed/EBRDo#subdirectory=python"

Stata

The most reliable route ships the reference data: clone the repo and put stata/ on the adopath.

* git clone https://github.com/angrahed/EBRDo.git
adopath ++ "EBRDo/stata"
help ebrdo

net install works for the program and help, but Stata treats the .dta reference data as ancillary (not copied to the adopath), so the clone route above is recommended:

net install ebrdo, from("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angrahed/EBRDo/main/stata") replace
* then fetch and place the datasets on your adopath (e.g. PERSONAL):
net get ebrdo, from("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angrahed/EBRDo/main/stata") replace

Quick start

# Julia
using DataFrames, EBRDo
df = DataFrame(country = ["Kazakhstan", "Germany", "Kosovo"])
ebrdo(df, :country)                      # adds the five columns
is_ebrd_coo("Kazakhstan")                  # 1
ebrd_name("TUR")                           # "Türkiye"
ebrd_coos()                                 # all 41 COO names, in reference order
# R
library(EBRDo)
df <- data.frame(country = c("Kazakhstan", "Germany", "Kosovo"))
ebrdo(df)                                # country column auto-detected
ebrd_region(c("DEU", "POL"), comparators = "Advanced Economies")
ebrd_coos()                              # all 41 COO names, in reference order
# Python
import pandas as pd, ebrdo
df = pd.DataFrame({"country": ["Kazakhstan", "Germany", "Kosovo"]})
ebrdo.ebrdo(df)                          # country column auto-detected
ebrdo.ebrd_name("TUR")                   # "Türkiye"
ebrdo.ebrd_coos()                        # all 41 COO names, in reference order
* Stata
ebrdo country, comparators("Advanced Economies")

Each port supports the same options (comparators, advanced, abbreviate, output naming), documented in its folder's README and in the Julia/R/Stata help. Input is matched case- and accent-insensitively; ISO2, ISO3, ISO-numeric, and name all resolve, and Kosovo (which has no official ISO3) is accepted as KOS, XKX, XK, KV, "Kosovo", and so on.

Repository layout

EBRDo/
├── julia/   EBRDo.jl    Julia package (depends on CountryCodes.jl)
├── r/       EBRDo       R package (CRAN-style; tibble/data.table/duckdb)
├── python/  ebrdo       Python package (pandas; depends on country_converter)
├── stata/   ebrdo       Stata package (ado + help + bundled crosswalk)
├── CITATION.cff
└── LICENSE  (MIT)

Citing

See CITATION.cff, or cite as: Anton Grahed, EBRDo: Harmonize countries in the EBRD style (Julia, R, and Stata), 2026.

Acknowledgements

Country code and name harmonization is powered by Vincent Arel-Bundock's countrycode (R) and its Julia port CountryCodes.jl; the Python port uses country_converter.

License

MIT © Anton Grahed.

angrahed/CountryCodes.jl.description: A Julia port of the R countrycode package: convert between country coding schemes and standardize country names.
angrahed/CountryCodes.jl.readmeHtml:
A Julia port of the R countrycode package. Convert between country coding schemes (ISO, CoW, Polity, IMF, WB, V-Dem, Eurostat, …) and standardize multilingual country names.

Status: pre-release. API may change.

Quick start

using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/angrahed/CountryCodes.jl")  # TODO: update once registered

using CountryCodes

countrycode("USA", :iso3c => :cown)                    # -> 2
countrycode(["USA", "DZA"], :iso3c => :cown)           # -> [2, 615]
countrycode("Albania", :country_name_en => :iso3c)     # -> "ALB"
countrycode("Congo-Kinshasa", :country_name_en => :iso3c)  # -> "COD"
standardize_name("Deutschland")                        # -> "Germany"
guess_field(["USA", "CAN", "MEX"])                     # -> :iso3c

Tables.jl integration

Works with any Tables.jl-compatible input — DataFrame, DuckDB.DBInterface results, CSV.File, Arrow.Table, named tuples of vectors, … Lookup runs once per unique source value, not once per row.

using DataFrames, CountryCodes

df = DataFrame(iso3c = ["USA", "DZA", "FRA"])

# Out-of-place: returns a column-table that round-trips to your input type.
DataFrame(add_country_codes(df, :iso3c => :cown))
# 3×2 DataFrame  iso3c=[USA,DZA,FRA]  cown=[2,615,220]

# In-place on a DataFrame:
add_country_codes!(df, :iso3c => [(:cow_code => :cown),
                                   (:name     => :country_name_en)])

10,000-row ISO3 → CoW conversion completes in well under 1ms after warmup.

Why GPL-3?

The upstream R countrycode package is GPL-3 licensed and we redistribute its data verbatim, so this port is also GPL-3. If you need a permissive-licensed package that only covers ISO codes, see Countries.jl.

Comparison

Package Schemes License Name regex matching Panel data
CountryCodes.jl 40+ (ISO, CoW, Polity, IMF, …) GPL-3.0 Yes Yes
Countries.jl ISO only MIT No No

Documentation

See docs/src/ for now. Hosted docs land in Phase 11.

License

GPL-3.0-or-later. See LICENSE.

angrahed/WBData.jl.description: A Julia client for the World Bank Open Data API: full pagination, tidy DataFrame returns, cached metadata, and local search.

lastCommit.message: Initial commit: WBData.jl, a paginating Julia client for the World Bank Open Data API

angrahed/WBData.jl.readmeHtml:
A Julia client for the World Bank Open Data API. It does for Julia roughly what R's wbstats does, and it's meant to replace WorldBankData.jl: full coverage of the API, tidy DataFrame returns, no hidden row caps, and a test suite that runs without touching the network.

Why not WorldBankData.jl?

WorldBankData.jl doesn't paginate. It sets per_page once and throws away anything that doesn't fit in a single response, which caps a query at about 25,000 rows. WBData.jl reads the page count from the response metadata and fetches the remaining pages at the same time. Ask for population across every country and aggregate from 1960 to today (around 16,000 rows) and all of it comes back, with nothing quietly dropped.

Installation

] add https://github.com/angrahed/WBData.jl

Quick start

using WBData

# Real countries (default), 1960 to 2023, joined with country metadata.
df = WBData.data("SP.POP.TOTL"; date = 1960:2023)

# Include aggregates (WLD, EUU, HIC, …):
df = WBData.data("SP.POP.TOTL"; country = :all, date = 1960:2023)

# Multiple indicators are fetched concurrently.
df = WBData.data(["SP.POP.TOTL", "NY.GDP.MKTP.CD"];
                 country = ["USA", "GBR", "FRA"],
                 date = 2000:2023)

# Most recent 5 values per series.
df = WBData.data("NY.GDP.MKTP.CD"; mrv = 5)

# Quarterly data: freq sets both the date format and the URL.
df = WBData.data("DPANUSSPB"; country = "USA", date = 2010:2020, freq = :quarterly)

# Wide layout: one column per indicator id, indexed by (iso3c, iso2c, country, date).
dfw = WBData.data(["SP.POP.TOTL", "NY.GDP.MKTP.CD"];
                  country = "USA", date = 2010:2023, wide = true)

The default long-format return has columns (iso3c, iso2c, country, indicator_id, indicator, date, value, unit, obs_status, last_updated) (plus the enrichment columns region, income_level, lending_type, and capital_city when enrich=true, and country_id, which carries the World Bank internal code that sometimes differs from the real ISO-2).

Metadata

WBData.indicators()      # ~17K rows, cached for 7 days
WBData.countries()
WBData.topics()
WBData.sources()
WBData.regions()
WBData.income_levels()
WBData.lending_types()
WBData.languages()

Every metadata call caches to disk through Scratch.jl. The default TTL is 7 days; change it with WBData.set_cache_ttl!(Day(1)).

Search

WBData.search_indicators("gdp per capita")
WBData.search_indicators(r"^SP\.POP")           # regex
WBData.search_indicators("school"; topic = 4)   # filter by topic id

WBData.search_countries("franc")

Search runs locally over the cached metadata, so it makes no extra API calls.

Configuration

WBData.set_default_language!("es")
WBData.set_user_agent!("MyProject/1.0 (me@example.com)")
WBData.set_timeout!(60)

These persist across sessions through Preferences.jl.

Cache management

WBData.cache_info()                # what is cached, plus age and size
WBData.clear_cache!()              # delete all metadata caches
WBData.clear_cache!("indicators_en")
WBData.set_cache_ttl!(Day(14))

Only metadata is cached; observations never are. Indicator and country listings rarely change, so a TTL of a few days is usually fine.

Errors

Errors are typed, and the API's habit of returning HTTP 200 with the error buried in the JSON body never reaches you as a surprise:

  • WBData.WBAPIError when the API returns an error payload.
  • WBData.WBNotFound when a metadata lookup matches nothing.
  • WBData.WBNetworkError when the retries run out (3 attempts, exponential backoff).
  • WBData.WBParseError when the response isn't the JSON we expected.

Migrating from WorldBankData.jl

WorldBankData.jl WBData.jl
wdi("SP.POP.TOTL", "US") WBData.data("SP.POP.TOTL"; country = "USA")
wdi(["A","B"], "all", 2000, 2020) WBData.data(["A","B"]; date = 2000:2020)
search_wdi("indicators", "name", r"...") WBData.search_indicators(r"...")
(no equivalent) WBData.data(...; mrv = 5)
(no equivalent) WBData.data(...; gapfill = true)
(no equivalent) WBData.data(...; freq = :quarterly)

Development

julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'
julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test()'

Tests are mocked end to end, so they need no network. Set ENV["WBDATA_INTEGRATION"] = "1" to also run the optional live-API checks.

License

MIT.
